To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fear-avoidance cognitions and pain-related fear are associated with pain-related disability, but that endurance cognitions and pain/task persistence behavior are not associated with pain-related activity limitations.
fear-avoidance cognitions and behaviors are associated with pain and physical disability, whereas endurance responses are associated with pain persistence and specific strain postures.
fear-avoidance cognitions and behavior as well as pain persistence behavior are associated with pain and pain-related outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of cognitions and behavior patterns that may be associated with pain-related disability and with the identification of subgroups of chronic musculoskeletal patients that may be at risk for the development of chronic pain.
the question of whether and to what extent the occurrence and persistence of pain responses can be explained by the interaction of cognitive, affective and behavioral variables.
the question of how to help people in pain to cope with their pain and disability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need for more studies on the association between pain responses and objectively measured physical activity in patients with musculoskeletal pain.
fear-avoidance is not the only pain response that should be considered in clinical practice.
the avoidance-endurance response model has been a valuable framework to guide research and clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pain-related cognitions and behaviors can be used to predict future pain-related disability and that these cognitions and behaviors are potentially modifiable targets for treatment.

fear-avoidance behavior is a major factor of disability in patients with musculoskeletal pain and that the development of different behavioral patterns of endurance responses is a consequence of the initial fear-avoidance response.
the avoidance-endurance responses model of pain is an important framework for understanding pain-related disability and for developing targeted interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fear-avoidance is not the only factor to target in pain management, and endurance-related responses may also be relevant.

there is a need to develop a more differentiated understanding of patients' pain-related cognitions and behaviors and to investigate the role of these cognitions and behaviors in the development of disability and the maintenance of pain.
the endurance-avoidance model provides a framework for understanding the role of cognitions, emotions, and behaviors in the development and maintenance of disability in chronic pain patients.
